stem.text: The power series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\left(x - 2\right)^{n}}{3^{n} n^{2}} \) has radius of convergence \( 3 \). Determine whether the series converges or diverges at \( x = -1 \), naming the test used.

answer_key.label: At \( x = -1 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) decrease to 0.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 2\right| < 3 \), so the left endpoint is \( x = -1 \).
At \( x = -1 \), \( \frac{\left(x - 2\right)^{n}}{3^{n}} = \left(\frac{-3}{3}\right)^{n} = (-1)^{n} \), so the series becomes \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n}}{n^{2}} \).
The terms alternate in sign, their sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) decrease as n increases, and \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2}} = 0 \).
At \( x = -1 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) decrease to 0, so \( x = -1 \) belongs to the interval of convergence.

options.label: At \( x = -1 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because \( \frac{1}{n^{2}} = 0 \).
options.derivation: the limit of the sizes written as an equation without limit notation, so the term itself is set equal to 0

options.label: At \( x = -1 \) the series diverges by the ratio test, because \( -1 < x < 5 \) leaves it out.
options.derivation: the endpoint never examined: the open interval from the ratio test taken as the whole answer

options.label: At \( x = -1 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2}} = 0 \).
options.derivation: the alternating series test applied with only the limit condition, the decrease of the sizes never stated
